findings.text: A batch naming two or more plans' landing records writes each record as it is reached, so a later record's refusal leaves the earlier records already written while the call reports ok=false and the plan write is discarded; measured against the pre-fix commit, where the same refused batch wrote nothing. Repro: driver /tmp/review-evid-append/repro.py, both logs in the run directory, control arm (fresh second anchor) writing both records in each.

The comment asserts a refused batch writes no record at all, and the test named for a refused batch holds only one record, so the cross-record case is unasserted and the wider claim is false at the reviewed head once two records are named.

item_verdicts.diff: read git diff e731091f..5ca9701f; the fix replaces a two-phase helper (validate every append, then write) with a per-record loop reading, applying and replacing each record inside that record's lock, which fixes the same-record overwrite and drops the cross-record pre-validation.
item_verdicts.done_when: read tests/test_edit_plan_append_evidence.py at 5ca9701f; the four §2 assertions are present (creation with the required meta, append beside an existing anchor, duplicate-anchor refusal naming the anchor, reckon audit-doc exit 0 on the created record) plus the batch, body-shape and concurrent-writer tests the fix added.
item_verdicts.goal: read the plan's §2 bullets against reckon/_store.py:606-720 at 5ca9701f; the op creates the record with reckon-type=evidence and plan-evidence-for, appends one anchored section before the closing main element, and refuses a duplicate anchor by name, but a batch naming several plans' records no longer leaves every record untouched when a later append is refused.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed run's manifest at the reviewed head; it records the three commits, the gate command with its result, the logs, and the declared batch mutation, with status complete.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the three commits against the declared paths; every changed path lies inside them and the op reaches the store through _OP_DISPATCH, not through reckon/mcp.py.

justifications.durability: three commits carry the op and its tests in the repository with gate, mutation and audit-demo logs beside the run, but the refusal path's partial write leaves no durable record of what the refused batch already wrote.
justifications.evidence: the diff, both batch tests and the concurrency test are on disk, and the review reproduced a refused multi-record batch against each arm of the fix (repro.log, repro-pre-fix.log), but no test in the change covers a batch naming two records.
justifications.fit: the op belongs in the store beside the section writes and reuses the shared path lock, but the fix removed a documented all-or-nothing property without a test or a note in the plan's landed summary.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/_store.py:675-714 implements all three §2 bullets and the refusals are tested, but the reviewed head's own behaviour contradicts the assertion at tests/test_edit_plan_append_evidence.py:248.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path lies in the declared write paths, reckon/mcp.py is untouched, and the one deletion in the diff is the replaced helper's own body.
